title: A Realistic Scorecard Timeline for a New Suppliers’ First 6 Months
summary: Learn what on-track supplier performance looks like in your first two quarters and how to use grace periods to protect your retail margins.
body_markdown:
In this article, learn about:


-


Why scorecards are diagnostic tools rather than immediate penalty mechanisms, and how retailers build baseline windows for supplier adjustment


-


The hidden data gaps in supplier portals and how they trigger early scorecard failures


-


A month-by-month guide to what performance actually looks like in your first two quarters


For emerging brands, securing a retail partnership is a major milestone. But as shipping begins, excitement is met with a high-stakes reality check: the vendor scorecard. Logging into a portal for the first time can feel like looking at an unintelligible jumble of percentages, acronyms, and penalty notices.


When early numbers do not align with standard thresholds, it is easy to panic. However,[scorecards](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/your-first-vendor-scorecard-reading-fill-rate-otif-and-chargeback-metrics) are the foundation for a continuous, data-driven conversation about supply chain execution. Understanding how to read these metrics over time, distinguishing between typical stumbles and chronic issues, and recognizing how major retailers build ramp-up time into their programs is what separates suppliers who scale from those who struggle.


## The Trajectory Mindset vs. The Instant Threshold


A common mistake is evaluating early scores against mature benchmarks. An established supplier with years of experience maintaining a 96% on-time in-full (OTIF) rate is playing a different game than a brand sitting at 75% in month two.


Thankfully, retail buyers understand this learning curve and design onboarding frameworks to accommodate the initial transition. A prime example of this ramp-up structure is the new-supplier grace period. Walmart, for example, offers new suppliers a three-month window where OTIF fines are waived while performance is actively tracked. This allows your operations team to troubleshoot electronic data interchange (EDI) connections and carrier handoffs without suffering margin-draining penalty invoices from day one.


Similarly, large-scale compliance programs often utilize phased rollouts. When Walmart introduced its[Supplier Quality Excellence Program (SQEP)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/sqep-and-its-defects) , it did so over a prolonged schedule, starting with purchase order accuracy before introducing barcode, labeling, and packaging phases in later periods. Well-designed programs also leverage initial baseline periods of 60 to 90 days before scoring officially starts to establish mutual accountability.


**Related Reading** :[How to Navigate Walmart's OTIF Scorecard in Retail Link](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/navigating-walmarts-new-otif-scorecard-in-retail-link)


## Gaps in Setup vs. Physical Execution


When new suppliers review early scorecard failures, they often treat every defect as a physical logistics failure. If a shipment is flagged as late or short, the immediate reaction is to blame the warehouse team or the carrier. Yet, in your first six months, most scorecard errors are actually data setup gaps rather than physical execution failures.


A digital supply chain operates on parallel tracks: a physical flow of goods and a digital flow of data. Long before a pallet is loaded onto a truck, data must flow seamlessly to the retailer. If item files are misconfigured, EDI mappings are untested, or[advance shipping notices (ASNs)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/edi-856-ship-notice-manifest) are mistimed, the physical cargo is doomed to fail compliance checks.


Item file discrepancies in portals like[Item 360](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/unlock-your/item-360-101) or[PIM systems](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-is-product-information-management-pim-and-how-do-suppliers-use-it) create a compounding effect downstream. An incorrect carton weight or case pack dimension means automated sorting equipment will flag the delivery as non-compliant. Nailing your item configuration and EDI setups early establishes your baseline.


### Case Studies


This foundational setup has direct financial consequences. For example, when apparel manufacturer[Fruit of the Loom](https://www.spscommerce.com/resources/case-study-fruit-loom/) managed five separate EDI systems, onboarding a new retailer took up to six months. Consolidating onto a unified network dropped that timeline to six weeks.


Similarly, national third-party logistics provider[DM Fulfillment](https://www.spscommerce.com/resources/sps-commerce-case-study-dm-fulfillment/) reduced testing and go-live cycles from twelve weeks to hours. When operations are streamlined, staff hours saved are substantial.


Knife manufacturer[Benchmade](https://www.spscommerce.com/resources/case-study-benchmade/) automated retail orders and invoices, saving over 780 hours of manual data entry in its first year while improving order accuracy. Getting your digital infrastructure in place before the first purchase order (PO) arrives ensures early scorecard stability.


## The First Six Months


To evaluate your business fairly, look at your trajectory over your first two quarters rather than a single weekly snapshot.


### Months 1–2: The Integration Baseline


Your goal in the first 60 days is addressing systemic data gaps and establishing your diagnostic baseline. Typical stumbles include missing[PO acknowledgment](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/purchase-order-acknowledgement-poa-spsa) windows, such as Ulta's two-business-day timeline, or sending misaligned ASNs.


Treat these weeks as a diagnostic sandbox. If your OTIF is sitting at 75%, do not panic. Instead, use the scorecard to identify whether the root cause is a recurring carrier delay or an incorrect item record. For distributors like[KeHE under its GBB 2.0 scorecard](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/a-suppliers-guide-to-kehes-good-better-best-gbb-20-brand-scorecard) , performance represents 25% of your overall grade, with fill rate representing half of that category's weight. Under KeHE's program, new brands are given a full year to align with onboarding expectations. Use this window to refine digital transmissions before penalty fees begin.


### Months 3–4: Root Cause Stabilization


As grace periods wind down, your performance must show upward progress. If your scorecard continues to show flat trends, the retailer will begin to interpret these stumbles as chronic operational limitations.


Tracing defects back to their origin is key at this stage. For example,[suppliers working with UNFI](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-to-become-a-supplier-for-unfi) should check if their carrier is missing appointments at the distribution center (DC). Conventional supplier appointments require 72 hours' notice, while Natural supplier appointments require 24 hours’ notice. Late arrivals at UNFI carry a $250 fee and cost you your scheduled dock slot, causing further receiving delays.


For[O'Reilly Auto Parts](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/oreilly-vendor-guide-requirements) , suppliers must maintain a 93% OTIF score to avoid a 15% fine on expected expenses. If you are above 93% but have late orders, you face a $100 fine per late PO. Pinpointing these specific bottlenecks keeps your score climbing.


It is important to note the necessity of keeping your focus on your compliance score rather than the dollar amount lost to deductions. Having a solid compliance performance score relative to your category competitors can make a big difference when it comes to line-reviews. And ultimately, a better compliance score will correlate to less money lost to deductions.


**Related Reading** :[Distributor Compliance Best Practices](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/distributor-compliance-best-practices)


### Months 5–6: Operational Mastery


By month six, your supply chain should operate with predictable, repeatable habits. Your operations team should no longer be debugging EDI connections; instead, they should be optimizing physical execution.


[Pallet](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/pallet-building-101-ti-hi-stacking-and-why-retailers-care) stability and[labeling](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/labeling-for-new-suppliers-gs1-128-sscc-and-where-labels-have-to-go) must be consistent. For[Costco](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/costco-supplier-requirements) in-club sales, display pallets must be durable and support 1,500 pounds for loads under 750 pounds, or up to 2,500 pounds on the bottom layer for heavier pallets. If you ship to[Kohl's](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-to-stay-compliant-with-kohls) , shipments must match ASNs within a strict 1% audit failure threshold to earn a high shipping performance grade and avoid post-audits. Weekly shipments to Kohl's must also be consolidated and sent to a single designated DC to maintain compliance.


## The First Two Quarters: An Operational Self-Check


To ensure your brand stays on the right trajectory, run this operational self-check each month before sitting down with your buyer:


-


Are we acknowledging every PO within the required window?


-


Does our item data in retailer portals match physical case pack sizes, avoiding automated setup defects?


-


Are our warehouses or 3PLs building pallets with proper label placement, clear stretch wrap, and correct stacking strength?


-


Is our performance trend showing monthly improvement, or is execution flat-lining as order volumes increase?


Mastering these requirements turns an emerging supplier into a reliable, long-term partner. By establishing clean digital handoffs and utilizing your early quarters to eliminate systemic defects, you protect your hard-earned margins, preserve shelf space, and build a foundation for sustainable growth.
